stem: The graph of the linear function \(f\) is shown in the \(xy\)-plane. The graph of \(y = g(x)\) is the reflection of the graph of \(y = f(x)\) across the \(x\)-axis. Which equation defines \(g\)?
solution: From the points \((0, 3)\) and \((4, -3)\), the slope of \(f\) is \(\frac{-3 - 3}{4 - 0} = -\frac{3}{2}\), so \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{2}x + 3\).
Reflecting across the \(x\)-axis changes every \(y\)-value to its opposite, so \(g(x) = -f(x) = \frac{3}{2}x - 3\).
Check: \((0, 3)\) becomes \((0, -3)\) and \((4, -3)\) becomes \((4, 3)\), and both lie on \(y = \frac{3}{2}x - 3\).

explanation.B: Incorrect. This changes the sign of the \(y\)-intercept only. The reflection changes the sign of every \(y\)-value, so the slope changes sign too.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This is \(f(-x)\), the reflection of the graph across the \(y\)-axis, not the \(x\)-axis.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This uses the reciprocal of the slope and keeps the \(y\)-intercept; a reflection across the \(x\)-axis does not invert the slope.

verify:
x = symbols('x')
p = figure['points']
m = Rational(p[1]['y'] - p[0]['y'], p[1]['x'] - p[0]['x'])
f = m*(x - p[0]['x']) + p[0]['y']
assert simplify(f - sympify(figure['curves'][0]['expr'])) == 0
g = expand(-f)
rhs = lambda s: value(s.split('=')[1])
assert [k for k in choices if simplify(rhs(choices[k]) - g) == 0] == [answer] == ['A']
